minimalCompletenessFindings: The rubric separates formula-only work (0), qualitative direction and magnitude comparisons with a correct zero (4.5), and full signed computations (10). It protects against systematic unsigned reasoning and repeated double subtraction (7 each), and it leaves room for an isolated arithmetic, sign or unit slip (9.5). Its minimum passing performance is nevertheless incomplete: a learner can declare the axis, give all four signed momenta and complete just I for 8.5, or omit units as well for 8. The missing cancellation is a requested calculation, not an optional interpretation. Conversely, correct directed values with a matching total can establish the combination without an explicit plus sign or explanatory sentence. A scientifically false extra assertion matters to scoring when it changes the requested quantities, as the false rest claim does in S36d15d5d6c.
